title: Is a Fast Boat Ride Bumpy, and Is It OK With Back or Neck Problems?
description: A fast boat can be bumpy, most of all at the front. With back or neck trouble, ask your doctor, sit at the back, pick a calm day and ask for a slow pace.
heroAlt: A guest's hand on a steel grab rail at the rear seat of a small boat
keywords: is a fast boat ride bumpy
where to sit on a boat to avoid bumps
can I ask for a slow boat ride

images.prompt: Late morning on a calm sea west of Funchal, Madeira. Taken from the rear seat of a white 9 metre motor boat with grey cushioned seats and a dark canopy, looking forward along the length of the boat. In sharp focus in the foreground, a guest's hand, no face, rests on a stainless steel grab rail beside a grey cushion. Beyond it the deck, the canopy frame and the bow, slightly raised as the boat moves at an easy pace, then a smooth deep blue sea and the brown wall of Cabo Girão far ahead in soft haze. Realistic photograph, natural colours.
images.alt: A guest's hand on a steel grab rail at the rear seat of a small boat

images.prompt: Seen from water level about 30 metres to the side: a white motor boat with a dark canopy moving slowly on a glassy, almost flat sea off the south coast of Madeira in early morning, a small smooth bow wave, two guests seen small from behind sitting at the stern. Realistic photograph, natural soft light.
images.alt: A small boat moving slowly on a glassy sea off Madeira in the early morning

images.prompt: Close detail on the deck of a small white motor boat in morning light: a guest's two feet in trainers set flat on the grey non-slip deck, knees relaxed, one hand resting on a knee, the edge of a grey cushioned seat and blue sea moving past in soft focus. Realistic photograph, no face.
images.alt: A guest's feet flat on the boat deck and knees relaxed for a softer ride
